use: Stresses something happened way earlier than the other person thinks.

example.romaji: Sonna no tokku ni shitteru yo.
example.ja: そんなのとっくに知ってるよ。
example.english: I've known that for ages.

examplePolite.romaji: Sore wa tokku ni shitte imasu yo.
examplePolite.ja: それはとっくに知っていますよ。
examplePolite.english: I've known that for a long time.

notes: Stronger than mou, 'already', often with a hint of 'obviously'.

use: Points to a way of doing or saying something just mentioned.

example.romaji: Sonna fuu ni iwanai de yo.
example.ja: そんなふうに言わないでよ。
example.english: Don't say it like that.

examplePolite.romaji: Sonna fuu ni iwanai de kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: そんなふうに言わないでください。
examplePolite.english: Please don't put it that way.

notes: Konna fuu ni is 'like this'; dou iu fuu ni asks 'in what way?'.

use: A firm, slightly formal 'eventually' for things bound to happen.

example.ja: いずれバレるよ。
example.english: It'll come out sooner or later.

examplePolite.romaji: Izure baremasu yo.
examplePolite.ja: いずれバレますよ。
examplePolite.english: It'll come out eventually.

notes: Sono uchi is vaguer and more casual.

use: Draws a conclusion from what you've seen or heard; usually ends with mitai or rashii.

example.ja: どうやら道を間違えたみたい。
example.english: Looks like we took a wrong turn.

examplePolite.romaji: Douyara michi o machigaeta you desu.
examplePolite.ja: どうやら道を間違えたようです。
examplePolite.english: It seems we've taken the wrong road.

use: From nakayoi, 'close'; nakayoku suru means to get along or be friends.

example.ja: 二人とも、仲良くしてね。
example.english: Play nice, you two.

examplePolite.romaji: Futari tomo, nakayoku shite kudasai ne.
examplePolite.ja: 二人とも、仲良くしてくださいね。
examplePolite.english: Please get along, you two.

notes: Kore kara mo nakayoku shite ne is a friendly 'let's stay friends'.

use: Says something happens and you can't explain why; common when telling stories.

example.ja: なぜか今日は眠れない。
example.english: For some reason I can't sleep tonight.

examplePolite.romaji: Nazeka kyou wa nemuremasen.
examplePolite.ja: なぜか今日は眠れません。
examplePolite.english: For some reason, I can't sleep tonight.

notes: Nazeka is about an unexplained fact; nandaka is about a vague feeling.

english: now (when it's too late); after all this time
use: Complains that something comes far too late to matter.

example.ja: 今更謝っても遅いよ。
example.english: It's too late to apologize now.

examplePolite.romaji: Imasara ayamatte mo osoi desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 今更謝っても遅いですよ。
examplePolite.english: Apologizing now is too late.

notes: Imasara kikenai means it's too awkward to ask now, for things you should already know.

english: while you're at it; on the way; also
use: Tacks an extra task onto something already happening; a common way to ask small favours.

example.romaji: Konbini iku nara, tsuide ni gyuunyuu katte kite.
example.ja: コンビニ行くなら、ついでに牛乳買ってきて。
example.english: If you're going to the store, grab some milk while you're at it.

examplePolite.romaji: Konbini ni iku nara, tsuide ni gyuunyuu o katte kite kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: コンビニに行くなら、ついでに牛乳を買ってきてください。
examplePolite.english: If you're going to the convenience store, could you pick up some milk too?

notes: Tsuide ni iu to means 'while I'm on the subject', adding a side point.

use: Making someone do something, or pushing something through, despite resistance.

example.ja: 無理やり連れてこられた。
example.english: I got dragged along against my will.

examplePolite.romaji: Muriyari tsurete koraremashita.
examplePolite.ja: 無理やり連れてこられました。
examplePolite.english: I was dragged here against my will.

notes: Also for forcing things, like cramming a bag shut or eating when you're full.

use: Softens bad news at the start of a sentence; a little formal.

example.ja: 残念ながら、売り切れだって。
example.english: Unfortunately, they say it's sold out.

examplePolite.romaji: Zannen nagara, urikire da sou desu.
examplePolite.ja: 残念ながら、売り切れだそうです。
examplePolite.english: Unfortunately, it seems they're sold out.

notes: In casual chat people often just say zannen! 'what a shame'.

english: before I knew it; without noticing
use: For changes that slipped by unnoticed, like time passing or something going missing.

example.romaji: Itsu no ma ni ka nechatta.
example.ja: いつの間にか寝ちゃった。
example.english: I fell asleep before I knew it.

examplePolite.romaji: Itsu no ma ni ka nete shimaimashita.
examplePolite.ja: いつの間にか寝てしまいました。
examplePolite.english: I dozed off without realizing.

notes: Totsuzen is a sudden event; itsu no ma ni ka is a gradual change you missed.

use: Stresses something has dragged on longer than it should, often with surprise or annoyance.

example.ja: いまだに信じられないよ。
example.english: I still can't believe it.

examplePolite.romaji: Imada ni shinjiraremasen.
examplePolite.ja: いまだに信じられません。
examplePolite.english: I still can't believe it.

english: just in case; to be safe
use: Explains a precaution or a double-check.

example.romaji: Nen no tame kasa motte ikou.
example.ja: 念のため傘持っていこう。
example.english: Let's take an umbrella just in case.

examplePolite.romaji: Nen no tame kasa o motte ikimashou.
examplePolite.ja: 念のため傘を持っていきましょう。
examplePolite.english: Let's bring an umbrella just in case.

notes: Nen no tame kakunin shimasu, 'let me just double-check', is common at work.

use: Choosing to do something unusual or harder on purpose, knowing the easy option.

example.ja: あえて何も言わなかった。
example.english: I deliberately didn't say anything.

examplePolite.romaji: Aete nani mo iimasen deshita.
examplePolite.ja: あえて何も言いませんでした。
examplePolite.english: I chose not to say anything.

notes: Unlike wazato, aete is a considered choice, not mischief.

english: for now; for a moment; once
use: Pauses or switches something temporarily before carrying on: stop for now, go home first.

example.ja: いったん家に帰るね。
example.english: I'll head home for now.

examplePolite.romaji: Ittan ie ni kaerimasu.
examplePolite.ja: いったん家に帰ります。
examplePolite.english: I'll go home first.

notes: Ittan kyuukei shiyou, 'let's take a break for now', is common in meetings and practice.

english: if by some chance; in the unlikely event
use: For a rare worst case you're preparing for, usually with -tara or no toki.

example.ja: 万が一遅れたら、連絡して。
example.english: If by some chance you're late, let me know.

examplePolite.romaji: Mangaichi okuretara, renraku shite kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 万が一遅れたら、連絡してください。
examplePolite.english: Should you be late, please let me know.

notes: Literally 'one in ten thousand'; mangaichi no toki means 'in an emergency'.

use: Almost always heard as douji ni, 'at the same time'.

example.ja: 同時に着いたね。
example.english: We got here at the same time.

examplePolite.romaji: Douji ni tsukimashita ne.
examplePolite.ja: 同時に着きましたね。
examplePolite.english: We arrived at the same time.

notes: Douji ni also links two facts: 'and at the same time...'.

use: When something turns out different from what you assumed, usually better or easier.

example.ja: 案外おいしいね、これ。
example.english: This is surprisingly good.

examplePolite.romaji: Kore, angai oishii desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: これ、案外おいしいですね。
examplePolite.english: This is surprisingly tasty.

notes: Igai to means the same and is a bit more common in speech.

use: Usually sono ba de, 'on the spot', for deciding, paying or reacting right there.

example.ja: その場で決めちゃった。
example.english: I decided right there on the spot.

examplePolite.romaji: Sono ba de kimete shimaimashita.
examplePolite.ja: その場で決めてしまいました。
examplePolite.english: I made the decision on the spot.

notes: Sono ba ni ita means 'I was there', present when it happened.

english: somehow; for no particular reason; vaguely
use: For choices and feelings you can't explain; on its own it's a full answer to 'why?'.

example.romaji: Nantonaku, kyou wa soto ni detakunai.
example.ja: なんとなく、今日は外に出たくない。
example.english: I just don't feel like going out today.

examplePolite.romaji: Nantonaku, kyou wa soto ni detakunai n desu.
examplePolite.ja: なんとなく、今日は外に出たくないんです。
examplePolite.english: For some reason, I don't feel like going out today.

notes: Nantonaku wakaru, 'I sort of get it', is a common half-yes.
